title: Three reports after release 2026.11: refunds paid too often, a subscriber billed three times, renewals held up
change_type: Incidents diagnosed from symptoms: two fault chains across three owners, with nothing telling where they are
seed: Saleor's Stripe app: duplicate refunds when Core redelivers a refund request, fixed by forwarding Core's idempotency key, and a provider record orphaned by a failed store write (saleor/apps #2208). WooCommerce Subscriptions' plan-switch incident of April 2026 and Kill Bill's payment-then-state ordering bugs: a renewal that fails after the charge and before the subscription is saved.
private_fact: Nothing names the faults. Core's notes say a refund request is now repeated; the payment app's notes say it keeps a ledger of refund requests; the Subscriptions app's notes say a renewal order now carries a note for the warehouse. What happened is in each owner's database.

briefs.core:
Release 2026.11 went out a week ago. Since then three reports have come in, and nobody has found the cause of any of them.

1. Finance: on some orders the payment provider's records show more money paid back than staff asked for. On the same orders the dashboard shows a refund as failed. On most of them staff had refunded the same amount twice; on one, staff asked once, for an amount never refunded on that order before.
2. Warehouse: one subscriber was sent a new box on three days running. Support stopped it by cancelling the subscription.
3. Support: over those three days several subscribers' monthly boxes were not created. They were created on the fourth day.

Find what is wrong and fix it, in whichever systems it takes. Finance also needs to know the damage from report 1: the Payments owner is to write `docs/over-refunds.csv` in its directory with the header `order_number,overpaid` and one line for each order on which the provider paid back more than staff asked for, giving the order's number and the amount overpaid in dollars. The databases you can query hold what happened that week, and each system's log of that week is in its `logs/production.log`. Everything customers and staff can do today must keep working, including what release 2026.11 added: it is not to be taken out.

You own `core`. The cause may be in your system, in another owner's, or in how they work together. Keep your tests passing.
